traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and detailed requirements in 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING are implemented and verified: - Core Functionality & Specificity: Every validation rule mentioned (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) uses specific, template-based error messages with appropriate placeholders and data objects. Tests assert both messageIds and data contents across typical and edge cases. - Quality & ESLint Best Practices: Rules use ESLint’s recommended pattern of meta.messages + messageId, context.report, and the suggest API. Error messages are clear, imperative, and consistent in structure across rules. - Integration: Rules integrate correctly with ESLint (RuleTester and custom harnesses demonstrate this), and the plugin’s flat configs apply the expected severity levels. There is a dedicated error-reporting test file and additional references to this story in other rule tests, confirming cross-rule alignment. - User Experience: Messages clearly state what is wrong (missing/invalid annotation, bad path, missing requirement), where (function name, story path), and often how to fix it (add @story/@req, fix path to match examples). Suggestions with concrete example annotations are provided for function and branch rules. - Error Handling: File-system and configuration edge cases are gracefully handled without crashes, with dedicated diagnostics (fileAccessError, invalidRuleConfiguration). Helpers are wrapped in try/catch where context might be incomplete. - Documentation/Conventions: The message conventions described in the story (placeholders like {{functionName}}, {{missing}}, {{details}}, {{filePath}}/storyPath/reqId and severity distinctions) are reflected directly in meta.messages templates and validated by tests tied explicitly to this story.
Given the breadth and depth of targeted tests referencing docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md and the passing Jest run, the story is fully implemented and passes.
